bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to natural resources; appropriating money for all-terrain vehicle trails and studies.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. APPROPRIATION; ST. LOUIS COUNTY.

(a) $752,000 in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the all-terrain vehicle account in the natural resources fund to the commissioner of natural resources for a grant to St. Louis County for the following all-terrain vehicle (ATV) trail projects:

(1) $75,000 for the Alborn Dirt Devils Club to engineer, permit, and acquire right-of-way for the County Road 166 to Ostman Road ATV trail project;

(2) $480,000 for the Ranger Snowmobile/ATV Club to engineer and construct the Seven Beavers ATV trail project;

(3) $100,000 for the Twig Area Trail Riders ATV Club to permit, design, engineer, and acquire right-of-way for the Lumberjack to Brookston ATV trail; and

(4) $97,000 for the Quad Cities ATV Club to engineer, survey, test, and design the club trailhead project.

(b) This is a onetime appropriation and is available until June 30, 2028.

Sec. 2. APPROPRIATION; CITY OF DULUTH.

$200,000 in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the all-terrain vehicle account in the natural resources fund to the commissioner of natural resources for a grant to the city of Duluth and Head of the Lakes ATV Riders for a Duluth-area all-terrain vehicle route study to establish connectivity to and through the western part of the city of Duluth. This is a onetime appropriation and is available until June 30, 2028.
additions: (a) $752,000 in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the all-terrain vehicle account in the natural resources fund to the commissioner of natural resources for a grant to St. Louis County for the following all-terrain vehicle (ATV) trail projects:
(1) $75,000 for the Alborn Dirt Devils Club to engineer, permit, and acquire right-of-way for the County Road 166 to Ostman Road ATV trail project;
(2) $480,000 for the Ranger Snowmobile/ATV Club to engineer and construct the Seven Beavers ATV trail project;
(3) $100,000 for the Twig Area Trail Riders ATV Club to permit, design, engineer, and acquire right-of-way for the Lumberjack to Brookston ATV trail; and
(4) $97,000 for the Quad Cities ATV Club to engineer, survey, test, and design the club trailhead project.
(b) This is a onetime appropriation and is available until June 30, 2028.

$200,000 in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the all-terrain vehicle account in the natural resources fund to the commissioner of natural resources for a grant to the city of Duluth and Head of the Lakes ATV Riders for a Duluth-area all-terrain vehicle route study to establish connectivity to and through the western part of the city of Duluth. This is a onetime appropriation and is available until June 30, 2028.
